exposure: type of delivery (normal vaginal delivery, cesarean section under general anesthesia, cesarean section under spinal anesthesia, painless labor)
type of anesthesia (general anesthesia, spinal anesthesia)
cohort: The study included 720 children aged 4-18 years, comprising cases diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, or oppositional defiant disorder, and healthy siblings as controls, recruited from psychiatric clinics in Iran.
finding: Delivery under general anesthesia was significantly associated with a 2.74 times increased likelihood of developing behavioral disorders compared to normal vaginal delivery or cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
mod_finding: Cesarean section under general anesthesia was significantly associated with behavioral disorders compared to normal vaginal delivery or cesarean section under spinal anesthesia.
followup_time: Outcomes were assessed in children aged 4-18 years, implying a follow-up period ranging from 4 to 18 years after birth.
